claim_findings.passage: Plan assumes a stable UK economy with real GDP growth averaging 1.4% and a terminal base rate of 3.5%.
claim_findings.evidence: The claim's own quote is only 'We assume a stable UK economic environment with real GDP growth averaging 1.4%.' -- it says nothing about a terminal base rate. The 3.5% terminal rate is a separate sentence in seg-0005 and is already captured, correctly and with its own quote, by claim-045. So half of claim-044's claim_text is not supported by claim-044's quote, and duplicates claim-045.
claim_findings.recommendation: Trim claim-044's claim_text to the GDP assumption only, leaving the terminal-rate assumption to claim-045.

claim_findings.passage: Management stated it is focused on delivering a 100-million-pound in-year benefit in 2026 under a narrow definition of AI (generative and agentic AI only, excluding broader digital/AI-enabled initiatives), rather than extending that figure into a 2030 forecast.
claim_findings.evidence: Two small mismatches. First, classification is 'reported_fact' and status 'reported', but the statement is a commitment to deliver a benefit over the current year ('we would stay focused for now on delivering the 100 million in year benefit'), not a reported outcome -- the segment also confirms the figure is for 'this year', i.e. still in flight. Second, the claim carries no period even though its value is explicitly year-scoped (2026), which is the one place a reader would want the unambiguous label. The substance of the claim is a fair reading of seg-0036.
claim_findings.recommendation: Set period to '12 months to 31 Dec 2026' and consider classification 'management_guidance' with status 'forward_looking', consistent with how other in-plan targets in this run are typed.

claim_findings.passage: Group lending balances of £492 billion at end Q2 2026, up over £5 billion (1%) versus Q1.
claim_findings.evidence: Period labels on claims 011, 014 and 015 were standardised this round to '3 months to 30 Jun 2026', which correctly labels the flows (+£5bn lending, +£5bn deposits, +£25bn AUA) and now matches claim-013. But claims 011 and 015 also carry point-in-time stocks in their values (lending_balances_billions 492, aua_billions 251) that are balances as at 30 Jun 2026, not three-month flows, so a single flow label does not describe the whole claim. The claim_text disambiguates in both cases ('at end Q2 2026', 'to £251 billion'), so this is a labelling nuance rather than a misreading.
claim_findings.recommendation: Either split the stock out into its own 'as of 30 Jun 2026' claim, or leave as is and rely on claim_text; if left as is, keep the same convention across 011 and 015 as now.

outlook_findings.passage: Management declined to give a full 2030 AI revenue/cost quantification, citing uncertainty over customer adoption and regulatory approval as the two variables it cannot control, and promised more detail at the January 2027 year-end results — this is a disclosed, acknowledged gap rather than an omission we are inferring.

The only claim covering seg-0036 is claim-061, whose claim_text stops at the £100 million narrow-definition benefit and the refusal to extend it into a 2030 forecast; it does not carry the two stated reasons (customer adoption, regulatory approval) or the deferral to the January 2027 year-end results. All three details are accurate against seg-0036, but a reader of claims.json alone cannot verify any of them, and Python's citation check cannot flag a sentence with no citation on it.

outlook_findings.passage: The observable indicator would be hedge notional growing faster than the "pretty modest" pace management guided, or the market/refinancing-rate gap holding open rather than closing toward the plan's 3.7% assumption [claim-047]
outlook_findings.evidence: claim-047 establishes only the 3.7% refinancing-rate assumption and the at-least-50bps market gap. summary: Round 3, full review (review-diff.json auto-escalated: 9 claims changed and outlook-brief.md prose changed). Verdict pass_with_warnings: no high or critical findings. Source correctness, temporal integrity, injection scan and process compliance are all clean. Both peer web sources are genuine and pre-event, and the Standard Chartered quote now comes from reporter body text rather than the page's 'AI generated' bullet block. All nine changed or added claims are fair readings of their segments: claim-061 (£100m narrow-definition AI benefit), claim-062 (NIM plateau) and claim-063 (out-deliver, then back through the capital framework) each anchor a statement the brief previously asserted loose, claim-043 no longer withholds the six-to-eight-billion figure, and claim-055 no longer equates growth rates across different metrics. The brief's substantive reasoning holds up: the upside case traces a real chain from the 3.7% refinancing assumption through the analyst's mark-to-market estimate to Chalmers' own reply, the downside case names three distinct mechanisms including the non-conservative £200m remediation assumption, and counter-evidence (claim-051, claim-060, claim-062) is surfaced rather than dropped. Four medium findings remain and they all share one root cause, the same one round 2 identified and only partly closed: material statements that are true against the transcript but have no claim anchoring them, so the brief either leaves them uncited or attaches a claim id that merely resolves. Section 9's opening AI-deferral sentence is uncited and its specifics (customer adoption, regulatory approval, January 2027) are outside claim-061. The 'pretty modest' hedge notional guidance is attributed twice to claim-047, which covers only the refinancing rate. The analyst's 'light versus consensus' characterisation, which is the premise of the entire Section 9 discussion, has no claim and is attached in Section 9 to claim-041, management's own guidance. And Section 4's assertion that management has not assumed margin improvement persists cites claim-047 rather than claim-062 or the unclaimed seg-0011 'non-heroic assumptions in terms of our margins' line. Five lower findings follow, including two more seg-0015 phrases quoted without a claim ('reignited', 'progressively more, second half of the plan'), a 2027-specific cost figure drawn from a plan-average claim, an 'every metric disclosed' overreach in the base case, claim-044's claim_text asserting a terminal rate its own quote does not carry, and claim-061 lacking a period despite a year-scoped value.
